text:
maria: Hey — after the client lib shading + okhttp bump to 4.11 our streaming endpoint in PROD started throwing NoSuchMethodError / ClassCastException when reading chunks. anyone seen this pattern? stack trace points at okhttp3.internal.http2.Http2Stream but then Jackson/Gson code shows up too.

kevin: ugh. common culprits: (1) relocate/shade rules accidentally duplicating jackson/gson classes, (2) wrong interceptor order consuming body, (3) mismatch okhttp / okhttp-urlconnection versions. did you try reproducing locally? :thinking_face: 

maria: repro is flaky locally. happens under higher concurrency. logs: 
```
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonFactory.createParser(Ljava/io/InputStream;)Lcom/fasterxml/jackson/core/JsonParser;
 at com.company.sdk.JsonUtils.parse(JsonUtils.java:34)
 at com.company.sdk.StreamingClient$1.onResponse(StreamingClient.java:121)
Caused by: java.lang.ClassCastException: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.json.UTF8StreamJsonParser cannot be cast to com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonParser
```

elena: that error screams mixed jackson versions on classpath. shading/relocate can leave multiple copies if libs brought their own shaded bits. what build tool?

maria: gradle with shadowJar. we relocated okhttp3 -> com.company.vendor.okhttp and tried to relocate com.fasterxml.jackson.* to avoid collisions.

dan: relocating jackson is risky. better to exclude-jackson from shading and rely on single version at runtime. if you must relocate, use exact package relocate rules and test for ClassLoader leaks. Also check for kotlin module differences: if using Kotlin, need jackson-module-kotlin on the classpath.

kevin: another angle: interceptor order. if you have an interceptor that reads the response body (e.g., logging) before streaming handler, the stream may be consumed. For streaming you usually want networkInterceptor or call clone semantics. Example: 
```
// BAD: application interceptor reads body and replaces it
client.addInterceptor(new LoggingInterceptor());
// GOOD: add as network interceptor so original stream still available
client.addNetworkInterceptor(new LoggingInterceptor());
```

elena: also check OkHttp call timeout vs read timeout. streaming endpoints can hit call.cancel if callTimeout < streaming duration. set callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) for unlimited and manage on upper layer.

maria: interesting — the stack shows the parser class itself failing to cast. that feels like two JsonFactory implementations on classpath. how can I quickly verify?

dan: run `jdeps -v` or just dump classloader resources: 
```
// quick check in a failing container
Enumeration<URL> res = Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader().getResources("com/fasterxml/jackson/core/JsonFactory.class");
while (res.hasMoreElements()) System.out.println(res.nextElement());
```
If you get multiple jar URLs, you found the dupes.

kevin: For Gradle ShadowJar, typical rule: exclude jackson from relocation, or relocate only your internal packages. Example minimal relocate: 
```
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.company.internal', 'com.company.shadow.internal'
  // avoid relocating whole third-party packages
  // exclude 'com.fasterxml.jackson' to keep single jackson
}
```

maria: we did relocate `com.fasterxml.jackson` because of earlier JAR clashes with some enterprise libs. hmm. maybe revert and test. any runtime hotfix if we can't rebuild quickly?

elena: short term: set JVM system property to prefer one jar? Not reliable. You can add a thin bootstrap classloader tweak by placing the desired jackson jars early on classpath (docker image layering) so the classloader picks them first. That can buy time.

dan: also check transitive gson usage. If parts of the stack use Gson and others Jackson, shading both can cause collision. Prefer one canonical JSON lib in the runtime. For our SDK we use Jackson; set `exclude group: 'com.google.code.gson'` in the shadow plugin if gson pulled in by extras.

maria: thanks — I reverted jackson relocation in a branch and ran shadowJar locally, ran the jvm class dump and only one JsonFactory found. CI artifacts still show duplication though. maybe a plugin dependency injecting a shaded jackson.

kevin: track down which dependency includes shaded jackson with `gradle dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` and grep. look for `jackson-core` or shaded jars like `*-all.jar` that bundle jackson.

maria: quick followup — streaming oddness still appears intermittently even after fixing jackson duplication. stacktrace now shows EOFException in okhttp while parsing NDJSON frames. 

elena: NDJSON + OkHttp: ensure you're using Response.body().source() and not calling body().string(). .string() buffers whole body and closes stream. For chunked streaming, use BufferedSource and readUtf8LineStrict or readUtf8Line; honor keepAlive. Also set `client.connectionPool()` config and `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` if you have special retry logic that restarts stream unexpectedly.

kevin: also check `ReadTimeout` and server-side chunk keepalive. If server sends keepalive every N seconds, but client readTimeout < keepalive interval, OkHttp will close with EOF. Use `readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)` for no read timeout if you control upper timeouts.

maria: aha — we had readTimeout = 30s for the client and server can be quiet for ~45s between events. that would close the stream and our parser chokes. increasing readTimeout fixed the EOFs locally.

dan: summary checklist for you: 
- undo jackson relocation and prefer single jackson at runtime
- run classloader resource dump to find dupes
- grep runtimeClasspath for shaded jars bundling jackson/gson
- prefer networkInterceptor for non-consuming logging
- use BufferedSource for NDJSON, avoid body().string()
- adjust OkHttp readTimeout/callTimeout for streaming
- consider excluding Gson if not needed

maria: amazing — thanks everyone. I'll push a hotfix image with jackson relocation removed and readTimeout bumped and report back.
